set.body:
Why
Comparison and predicate families remain the clearest broad loss. Current paths pay generic offset traversal, Boolean writer abstraction, and for scalar comparisons sometimes scalar-array construction. These are reusable kernel taxes, not NumPy magic.

Scope
- Add dtype-specialized monomorphic comparison and predicate loops with one dispatch before traversal.
- Add scalar-specialized binary and comparison paths that do not construct rank-zero arrays or broadcast plans per call.
- Make contiguous and offset-contiguous Boolean output a direct JVM Boolean-array or Scala.js Uint8Array write; retain general strided fallbacks.
- Hoist stable shape, stride, broadcasting, writer, and predicate decisions out of the element loop.
- Keep Float, Double, integral, NaN, infinity, signed-zero, empty, scalar, broadcast, strided, transposed, and reversed semantics exact. Scala.js Long is correctness-only.

Generality guard
Selection may depend only on public semantic facts such as dtype, operation kind, rank, strides, contiguity, broadcasting, and alias state. Any dependency on benchmark case name, exact benchmark shape, or fixture identity rejects the change.

Acceptance
- Public comparison and predicate cases improve by at least 1.20x on their targeted class, with stronger family-level gains expected from removing per-element abstraction.
- No established public case regresses more than 10 percent without an explicit, evidence-backed tradeoff.
- Allocation evidence shows only required results plus bounded planning state.
- JVM and full-linked Node receipts cover multiple dtypes, sizes, and layouts; Node demonstrates direct typed-array loops for supported primitive storage.
- JVM and Scala.js laws, semantic signatures, and standard gates pass exactly.
set.title: Remove comparison, predicate, and scalar-loop taxes
